rv.q: On the other hand, he may simply be a bore.

Broderick, sporting a technically competent but unconvincing British accent, has worked this sort of territory too often to be interesting, and his one-note turn fails to convey his character’s hidden depths.

For sheer dullness, this putative comedy, directed by the talented David Grindley (“The American Plan”) for the Roundabout Theater Company and starring the talented but increasingly mannered Matthew Broderick, beats just about anything on Broadway this season.
David Grindley's production, by contrast, is as deep as a paddling pool.
You can still enjoy this otherwise amusing evening by viewing it around its star, but no audience member should be forced to work that hard.
A visit to this Philanthropist is like playing word games with a group of unpleasant new acquaintances.

cn.t: Critics find this Hampton revival moribund and irrelevant, with Broderick giving a weak, passive performance. The play traps audiences in a stuffy room with unpleasant academics engaged in dreary chatter that feels disconnected from reality.

vs.sum: Completed a major renovation in early 2026 with all seats replaced and legroom expanded, making it one of Broadway's most comfortable and modern houses. New restrooms significantly reduce intermission wait times.

acc.note: Elevators to all levels. 53 assistive listening devices. 11 wheelchair seats across Orchestra and Balcony.
